newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Thai PM pushes S.China Sea basin as growth centre.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM pushes S.China Sea basin as growth centre.

text.p: Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh on Thursday called for the transformation of the South China Sea basin into Asia's new growth zone.

Chavalit, on a visit to the Philippines, also said an expanded Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), which will include Cambodia, Burma and Laos, could become the growth engine for Asia and the world in the next century with its expected combined gross domestic product of $1.3 trillion.

"There will certainly be challenges and pitfalls along the way. If we want a place in the sun, we have to expect some blisters," he said. ASEAN currently comprises Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
Chavalit spoke to foreign and Filipino businessmen before leaving Manila for Bangkok at the end of a two-day visit to the Philippines highlighted by talks with President Fidel Ramos.

"The idea is to create a new economic growth zone stretching from the eastern seaboard of Thailand through Cambodia, Vietnam and southeast China to Subic Bay, Palawan Island and Iloilo city" in the Philippines, he said.
"This would help transform the South China Sea basin into a lake of cooperation and vibrant economic activity."
He said the Asian Development Bank (ADB) should be asked to undertake feasibility studies "to bring the idea to fruition".
Diplomats have described the South China Sea as a possible flashpoint because of rivalries for its potentially oil-rich islands, such as the Spratlys, among various nations.
The Spratlys are claimed wholly or in part by China, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines, Malaysia and Brunei.
Chavalit held talks with Ramos on Wednesday and also played a round of golf with him.
"We chased a small white ball around the course because we are too old to chase anything else," Chavalit said of the game. "But we can still dream.
"Our dream is to work closely together to position our respective nations to meet the challenges of the next century."
